kill_fact: The base fair value of $60 does not follow from the record's own sum-of-the-parts. The itemised parts are Indonesia about $23bn, North America about $40bn, South America about $11bn, Atlantic and other about $1bn, corporate about minus $5bn - a total of $70bn of attributable enterprise value. Less the $4.6bn of net debt the record itself assigns to Freeport's share, equity is $65.4bn, or $45.32 a share on 1,443m shares (share count confirmed in the 10-Q filed 2026-08-06); adding the record's own $6.90 a share of risked growth options gives $52.20, not $60. The record instead prints '$76 billion of equity or $52.50 a share', which requires an enterprise value of about $80.6bn (10.7 x 7.5) that none of its listed parts supports - the same line mislabels the blend as 7.5x when $70bn on $10.7bn attributable is 6.5x. The thesis is not killed: every load-bearing bear pillar verified against primary sources, and the arithmetic fix moves in the bear's direction (the shares are about 34% above corrected fair value at today's $68.35, not 12% above $60).
corrections: 1) BASE FV. Re-deriving the record's own parts schedule gives $52.20 a share, not $60 (see kill_fact). 2) EBITDA ANCHOR. The build assumes $17.8bn consolidated 2027-28 EBITDA at $6.20 copper, $4,000 gold, $30 moly. Freeport's own slide 10, presented on the 2026-07-23 second-quarter call on exactly those gold and moly assumptions, ladders annual EBITDA from about $13bn at $5.00 copper to about $20bn at $7.00, with sensitivity of about $390m per $0.10 - which puts $6.20 copper at $16.9bn to $17.7bn, midpoint about $17.3bn. The record's anchor is roughly 3% above the company's own published ladder; carried through the parts at the record's own multiples that is about minus $1.4 a share. 3) CERRO VERDE STAKE IS STALE. The record uses 53.56% with 46% minorities; on the 2026-07-23 call management disclosed that open-market purchases during the June 2026 quarter raised Freeport's holding by 2%, to over 55%. Worth about plus $0.2 a share at the record's 6.0x South America multiple - it works against the bear, and is the only correction that does. Net of 2) and 3), revised base fair value is $51. 4) BULL LEVEL MISCITES THE SAME SLIDE. The $90 build states the company's ladder shows about $24bn at $7.00 copper; the 2026-07-23 deck shows about $20bn at $7.00. Extrapolating the company's own $390m per $0.10 to the $7.50 the bull case assumes gives about $22.0bn, plus the roughly $1bn of leach uplift the record adds, equals about $23.0bn, not $24bn - which at the record's own 60% attributable share, 8.5x and $4.6bn net debt gives $78.1 plus $8 of options, or $86. 5) FREE CASH FLOW. The record's 'real trailing free cash flow closer to $1.7bn' is $1.86bn on the filings (trailing operating cash flow $5.919bn less capital spending $4.058bn), a 1.9% yield; first-half 2026 capital spending was $1.946bn, not $2.1bn, so first-half free cash flow was about $1.62bn, not $1.4bn. Directionally the bear's point stands: the scan's $5.92bn 'free cash flow' is operating cash flow with capital spending recorded as zero, confirmed. 6) CATALYST NOTE. The record says the Indonesian extension 'remains a memorandum'. On 2026-07-23 management disclosed that a formal extension application was submitted in June 2026 in accordance with the agreed terms. The licence is still not issued and no date has been published, so SOFT_EXTENDED stands, but the note is one milestone stale. 7) DRIFT. The 200-day averages moved: FCX $57.89 (record $57.10) and copper $5.856 (record $5.81) as of 2026-08-11.

corrections_typed.basis: Record's own parts (2026-08-04 sop_breakdown) sum to $70bn attributable EV; less its own $4.6bn Freeport-share net debt = $65.4bn equity / 1,443m shares (10-Q filed 2026-08-06) = $45.32, plus its own $6.90 of growth options = $52.20. Then minus $1.4 for the 3% overstated EBITDA anchor versus Freeport's slide-10 ladder of about $13bn at $5.00 and about $20bn at $7.00 copper with $390m per $0.10 (2026-07-23 call), plus $0.2 for the Cerro Verde stake raised to over 55% in the June 2026 quarter (same call) = $51.

evidence: Freeport-McMoRan Q2 2026 earnings call, 2026-07-23 (FMP transcript): 2026 average unit net cash cost estimate of $1.90 per pound, cut from the April estimate of $1.95; the 2027 United States cost target of $2.50 per pound reaffirmed but with energy, sulfur and acid prices described as taking that opportunity away in 2027; slide-10 modelled 2027-28 average EBITDA of about $13bn at $5.00 copper to about $20bn at $7.00 (gold held at $4,000, moly at $30), sensitivity about $390m of annual EBITDA per $0.10 of copper; 2027 capital expenditures raised to $4.8bn, about $300m above the April estimate, with discretionary spend of $1.6bn in 2026 and $1.9bn in 2027 and the Bagdad expansion excluded at a preliminary capital cost in the $4.5bn range, about 30% above the 2023 estimate; Cerro Verde ownership raised 2% to over 55% via open-market purchases; a formal Grasberg extension application submitted in June 2026 with no licence issued and no published date; Grasberg ramp reaffirmed at about 65% of capacity in the second half of 2026, 80% by mid-2027.

Freeport-McMoRan Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30, filed 2026-08-06 (FMP as-filed statements): revenue $7.029bn versus $7.582bn a year earlier; income from continuing operations $1.386bn of which only $984m attributable to Freeport shareholders (29% to non-controlling interests); non-controlling interests carried at $12.113bn; total debt $10.359bn including $973m of leases against $4.080bn of cash, net debt $6.279bn; weighted average shares 1,443m, unchanged over six quarters (no dilution).

Trailing twelve months to 2026-06-30 from the filed statements (10-Qs/10-K filed 2025-11-06, 2026-02-13, 2026-05-08, 2026-08-06): EBITDA $8.999bn; operating cash flow $5.919bn against capital spending $4.058bn, so real trailing free cash flow $1.86bn (the scan's $5.92bn 'free cash flow' is operating cash flow with capital spending recorded as zero, confirmed); attributable income was 64.3% of continuing-operations income, a 35.7% minority leakage, confirming the record's 36%.
